title: SSC CGL Tier-1 English (Eduquity Pattern) — Day 1: Set 1
subject: English Language

questions.q: The newly appointed chief executive officer has been working under the assumption that the quarterly revenue targets could be achieved without downsizing the operations department.
o: had been worked under the assumption
questions.e: The Present Perfect Continuous tense is correctly used for an action that began in the recent past and is still ongoing. The standard expression is “under the assumption.”
questions.instruction: Choose the option that provides the correct/improved form of the sentence.

questions.q: Identify the option that contains an incorrectly spelt word.
o: The corporate restructuring caused significant administrative inconvenience.
Superstitious beliefs often hinder the development of a scientific temperament.
The chef prepared an exquisite dessert featuring an assortment of exotic fruits.
The hypercritical analysis of the movie received widespread public critisism.
questions.e: The misspelled word is “critisism”; the correct spelling is “criticism.”
questions.instruction: Identify the option that contains an incorrectly spelt word.

target.meaning: The expression of disapproval or the analysis and evaluation of something.

options.A: Criticism: Correct spelling; the expression of disapproval or evaluation.
options.B: Critisism: Incorrect spelling; the correct spelling is “criticism.”
options.C: Critisizm: Incorrect spelling; the correct spelling is “criticism.”
options.D: Criticismm: Incorrect spelling; the correct spelling is “criticism.”

questions.q: The committee members, having spent over three hours deliberating the intricate nuances of the corporate merger, was explicitly reluctant to ratify the proposed clause despite the chairperson’s persuasive remarks.
o: The committee members, having spent over three hours
deliberating the intricate nuances of the corporate merger,
was explicitly reluctant to ratify the proposed clause
questions.e: The true subject is the plural noun “committee members,” so the verb must be plural: “were explicitly reluctant.”
questions.instruction: Identify the part of the sentence that contains a grammatical error.

questions.q: The lead defense attorney asked the prime witness, "Can you state with absolute certainty that you observed the suspect leaving the residential complex before midnight?"
o: The lead defense attorney asked the prime witness if he could state with absolute certainty that he observed the suspect leaving the residential complex before midnight.
The lead defense attorney asked the prime witness if he could state with absolute certainty that he had observed the suspect leaving the residential complex before midnight.
The lead defense attorney inquired from the prime witness that whether he can state with absolute certainty that he had observed the suspect leaving the residential complex before midnight.
The lead defense attorney asked the prime witness if he can state with absolute certainty that he observed the suspect leaving the residential complex before midnight.
questions.e: In indirect speech, “Can” changes to “could” after the past reporting verb “asked.” The earlier observation is appropriately represented by “had observed.” “Asked” takes “if/whether,” not “that whether.”
questions.instruction: Choose the correct indirect-speech form of the given question.

questions.q: In an era dominated by rapid globalization, maintaining an insular approach to foreign policy can severely alienate a developing country from its global allies. (Find Antonym)
questions.e: Insular means narrow-minded or uninterested in cultures and ideas outside one’s own experience. Cosmopolitan is its true antonym.

target.meaning: Ignorant of or uninterested in cultures, ideas, or peoples outside one's own experience; narrow-minded.

options.A: Parochial: Having a limited or narrow outlook or scope (synonym to Insular).
options.B: Cosmopolitan: Familiar with and at ease in many different countries and cultures (true antonym).
options.D: Prejudiced: Having or showing a dislike or distrust derived from fixed preconceived ideas.

questions.instruction: Choose the word that is opposite in meaning to the highlighted word “insular”.

questions.q:
Arrange the sentences in the most logical sequence:
P: While green energy sources like solar and wind power offer a sustainable alternative, their intermittent nature presents a significant operational hurdle for heavy industries.
Q: To resolve this grid instability, engineering firms are investing heavily in advanced lithium-ion battery storage infrastructure.
R: The global transition toward a carbon-neutral economy requires an immediate and massive overhaul of existing power grids.
S: Without these robust storage systems, manufacturing plants risk frequent operational blackouts during seasonal weather changes.
questions.e: R establishes the broad topic, P introduces the specific obstacle, Q presents the solution, and S gives the consequence of not using that solution. Hence, RPQS.
questions.instruction: Arrange P, Q, R and S in the most logical sequence.

questions.q: During the corporate crisis, the junior executives were told to keep their chin up as the management was actively working to secure an external bailout package.
o: To remain cheerful and optimistic in difficult circumstances
To stay vigilant against internal corporate espionage
To voice their complaints aggressively to the board
questions.e: “Keep your chin up” means to stay brave, hopeful, and resilient during difficult circumstances.

options.B: To remain cheerful and optimistic in difficult circumstances.
options.C: To stay vigilant against internal corporate espionage.
options.D: To voice complaints aggressively to the board.

questions.instruction: Choose the option that best expresses the meaning of the idiom “keep their chin up”.

questions.q: Despite of the unrelenting downpour and the subsequent waterlogging across the primary arterial roads, the dedicated medical staff managed to reach the emergency ward right on time.
o: and the subsequent waterlogging across the primary arterial roads,
the dedicated medical staff managed to reach
the emergency ward right on time.
questions.e: “Despite” is not followed by “of.” Use “Despite the unrelenting downpour” or “In spite of the unrelenting downpour.”
questions.instruction: Identify the part of the sentence that contains a grammatical error.

questions.q: The architectural firm meticulously designed the futuristic blueprint of the smart city to ensure optimal utilization of renewable energy resources.
o: The futuristic blueprint of the smart city was being meticulously designed by the architectural firm to ensure optimal utilization of renewable energy resources.
The futuristic blueprint of the smart city was meticulously designed by the architectural firm to ensure optimal utilization of renewable energy resources.
The futuristic blueprint of the smart city had been meticulously designed by the architectural firm to ensure optimal utilization of renewable energy resources.
To ensure optimal utilization of renewable energy resources, the futuristic blueprint of the smart city is meticulously designed by the architectural firm.
questions.e: Simple Past active changes to Object + was/were + V3 + by Subject. Hence, “was meticulously designed” is correct.
questions.instruction: Choose the correct passive-voice form of the sentence.

questions.q: The project coordinator said to the team members, "Do not compromise on the software quality checks, otherwise the deployment phase will face severe delays next month."
o: The project coordinator warned the team members not to compromise on the software quality checks, otherwise the deployment phase would face severe delays the following month.
The project coordinator told the team members to not compromise on the software quality checks, otherwise the deployment phase will face severe delays next month.
The project coordinator ordered the team members that they should not compromise on the software quality checks, otherwise the deployment phase would face severe delays next month.
The project coordinator warned the team members against compromising on the software quality checks, otherwise the deployment phase will face severe delays the following month.
questions.e: A negative imperative can be reported as “warned/told + object + not to.” “Will” changes to “would,” and “next month” becomes “the following month.”
questions.instruction: Choose the correct indirect-speech form of the given statement.

questions.q: A person who holds an unconventional, non-conformist, and independent view, especially in social, artistic, or political matters, refusing to follow the rules of a group.
questions.e: Maverick means an unorthodox or independent-minded person.

options.A: Maverick: An unconventional or independent-minded person. Synonyms: Nonconformist, Dissenter, Rebel. Antonyms: Conformist, Traditionalist, Conventionalist.
options.B: Altruist: A person concerned with the welfare of others. Synonyms: Philanthropist, Benefactor, Humanitarian. Antonyms: Egoist, Selfish person, Misanthrope.
options.C: Sycophant: A person who flatters someone important for personal advantage. Synonyms: Toady, Flatterer, Bootlicker. Antonyms: Critic, Detractor, Opponent.
options.D: Epicure: A person who takes particular pleasure in fine food and drink. Synonyms: Gourmet, Connoisseur, Epicurean. Antonyms: Ascetic, Abstemious person, Teetotaller.

questions.instruction: Choose the word that best fits the given description.

questions.q: Not only did the investigative journalist uncover a massive financial fraud involving the offshore accounts, but he also revealed how deeply entrenched corruption was in the administrative machinery.
o: Not only did the investigative journalist uncover
a massive financial fraud involving the offshore accounts,
but he also revealed how deeply entrenched
questions.e: The sentence correctly uses inversion after “Not only” and the correlative pair “not only ... but ... also.” There is no grammatical error.
questions.instruction: Identify the part of the sentence that contains an error. Choose (D) if there is no error.

questions.q: Identify the option that contains a spelling error within the given context.
o: The sovereign nation maintained its autonomy through strict diplomatic protocols.
The sudden obsolescence of the old manufacturing equipment paralyzed production.
The archeologist discovered a historical artifact that contradicted previous timeline hipotheses.
His magnanimous gesture toward his political rivals surprised the entire electorate.
questions.e: “Hipotheses” is incorrectly spelled; the correct spelling is “hypotheses.”

Sovereign.meaning: Possessing supreme or ultimate power; independent.

Obsolescence.meaning: The state of becoming outdated or no longer useful.

Hypotheses.meaning: Plural of hypothesis; proposed explanations based on limited evidence.

Magnanimous.meaning: Generous or forgiving, especially toward a rival.

questions.instruction: Identify the option that contains a spelling error.

questions.q: The magistrate noted that the evidence presented by the prosecution was entirely tenuous, lacking any substantive material to link the accused directly to the white-collar crime. (Find Synonym)
questions.e: Tenuous means very weak, slight, flimsy, or insubstantial. “Flimsy” is the true synonym.

target.meaning: Very weak, slight, flimsy, or insubstantial.

options.A: Formidable: Inspiring fear or respect through being impressively large, powerful, or intense (antonym).
options.B: Flimsy: Lacking strength or solidity; weak (true synonym).
options.C: Authentic: Of undisputed origin and genuine authenticity.
options.D: Equivocal: Open to more than one interpretation; ambiguous.

questions.instruction: Choose the word that is closest in meaning to the highlighted word “tenuous”.

questions.q: The diplomatic delegation decided to call off on the bilateral negotiations after the host country abruptly altered the pre-negotiated trade tariffs.
o: call out on the bilateral negotiations
questions.e: “Call off” means to cancel an event, meeting, or transaction. The extra “on” is incorrect.
questions.instruction: Choose the option that correctly improves the sentence.

questions.q: Had the meteorological department issued the emergency severe weather warning a few hours prior, the coastal administrative authorities would have successfully evacuated the vulnerable low-lying regions.
o: the emergency severe weather warning a few hours prior,
the coastal administrative authorities would have successfully evacuated
questions.e: This is a correctly formed third conditional in inversion: “Had + Subject + V3 ..., Subject + would have + V3.” There is no error.
questions.instruction: Identify the part of the sentence that contains an error. Choose (D) if there is no error.

questions.q: Analysts are closely monitoring the fluctuating patterns of the stock index to predict the upcoming economic correction.
o: The fluctuating patterns of the stock index are being closely monitored by analysts to predict the upcoming economic correction.
The fluctuating patterns of the stock index were closely monitored by analysts to predict the upcoming economic correction.
The fluctuating patterns of the stock index are closely monitored by analysts to predict the upcoming economic correction.
The upcoming economic correction is being predicted by analysts by closely monitoring the fluctuating patterns of the stock index.
questions.e: Present Continuous active changes to Object + is/are/am + being + V3 + by Subject. Hence, “are being closely monitored” is correct.
questions.instruction: Choose the correct passive-voice form of the sentence.

questions.q: The scientific research facility was forced to shut down its experimental project because the expected breakthroughs turned out to be a mere castle in the air.
o: A visionary but highly impractical plan
questions.e: “Castles in the air” means daydreams, plans, or grand designs with no practical basis or realistic possibility of success.

options.B: A visionary but highly impractical plan.

questions.instruction: Choose the option that best expresses the meaning of the idiom “castle in the air”.

questions.q:
Arrange the sentences in the most logical sequence:
P: This demographic shift has created an unprecedented demand for flexible healthcare policies that prioritize preventative care over emergency treatments.
Q: Furthermore, urban migration has compressed the available housing space, fundamentally altering family structures and support systems for the elderly.
R: Over the past two decades, the nation has witnessed a substantial transformation in its socio-economic landscape due to rapid industrial growth.
S: Consequently, municipal corporations are forced to re-evaluate their city planning layout to accommodate both commercial zoning and residential wellbeing.
questions.e: R introduces the macro theme, Q adds another development, P refers back to the demographic shift, and S gives the consequence. Hence, RPQS.
questions.instruction: Arrange P, Q, R and S in the most logical sequence.

questions.q: The professor’s lucid explanation of the complex thermodynamic principles allowed even the novice undergraduate students to grasp the core concepts effortlessly. (Find Synonym)
questions.e: Lucid means expressed clearly and easy to understand. “Transparent” is the intended contextual synonym.

options.A: Obscure: Not discovered or known about; uncertain or difficult to comprehend (antonym).
options.B: Transparent: Easy to perceive or detect; perfectly clear in meaning (true contextual synonym).
options.D: Comprehensive: Complete; including all or nearly all elements or aspects of something.

questions.instruction: Choose the word that is closest in meaning to the highlighted word “lucid”.

questions.passage: The rapid integration of Artificial Intelligence (AI) into modern legal systems has sparked an intense global debate among jurists and tech ethicists. While proponents argue that automated algorithms can drastically reduce case backlogs by quickly parsing millions of legal documents, critics raise concerns regarding algorithmic bias. Since machine learning models are trained on historical data, they inherently (21) the historical prejudices embedded within those past judicial rulings. This creates a feedback loop where systemic biases are not just maintained, but actively (22). Therefore, relying blindly on automated legal assistants could jeopardize the very core of (23) justice. Legal experts suggest that AI should never be allowed to operate with absolute autonomy; rather, it must serve as an auxiliary tool under strict human (24). Maintaining a "human-in-the-loop" framework ensures that ethical nuances and situational contexts are carefully weighed before arriving at a (25) legal verdict.

questions.e:
Since machine models train on historical human data, they naturally preserve and pass down old patterns. Perpetuate means to make something continue indefinitely.
Alleviate / Mitigate: To make a problem less severe.
Repudiate: To refuse to accept or reject something.
